newsitem.title: USA: Rhone-Poulenc submits application to FDA.
newsitem.headline: Rhone-Poulenc submits application to FDA.

text.p: Rhone-Poulenc Rorer Inc said Wednesday it submitted a supplemental new drug application to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration for a tablet formulation of a drug used to manage bed-wetting for children six years of age and older.
The company said the application covers DDAVP tablets, an oral version of the active ingredient in DDAVP nasal spray, which is prescribed by doctors to treat the childhood problem of bed-wetting.
Currently, the tablet version of DDAVP is cleared for use only for treating central diabetes insipidus.
DDAVP Tablets are manufactured for Rhone-Poulenc Rorer by Ferring Pharmaceuticals of Malmoe, Sweden.
